The results of this study suggest that the safest areas for the placement of miniscrews are between the first and second premolars and between the first and second molars in posterior mandibular sites. This is regardless of the angle of insertion.

This conclusion is supported by research on the factors affecting miniscrew placement, including bone thickness and inter-radicular space. In general, for optimal results, it's recommended to place miniscrews in areas with adequate bone density and minimal inter-radicular space. However, specific recommendations may vary depending on individual patient conditions.

In posterior mandibular sites, where the bone is typically thinner and more complex than other areas, placing miniscrews between the first and second premolars or molars can be a safer option. Additionally, maintaining a healthy bone thickness and avoiding excessive inter-radicular space are crucial for successful miniscrew placement.

While there may not be a single definitive answer to whether bone thickness and inter-radicular space affect miniscrew placement in all cases, this study suggests that these factors play a role in determining the safest areas for miniscrew placement.
